Procedures.title: The right procedure for your body — not a one-size plan.
Procedures.titleShort: The right procedure for your body.
Procedures.aside: Every patient starts with a full assessment. Together, we choose the option that fits your health, your goals and your life.

sleeve.name: Sleeve gastrectomy
sleeve.desc: Removes the larger part of the stomach, reducing how much you can eat and the hunger hormone it produces.
sleeve.descShort: Removes the larger part of the stomach to reduce appetite and intake.
sleeve.meta: Stay [X days] · Back to work [X weeks]

bypass.name: Gastric bypass
bypass.desc: Full or partial (mini) bypass: a small stomach pouch is connected directly to the small intestine.
bypass.descShort: Full or partial bypass — a small pouch joined to the small intestine.
bypass.meta: Stay [X days] · Back to work [X weeks]

plication.name: Gastric plication
plication.desc: The stomach is folded inward and stitched to reduce its volume — no part of the stomach is removed.
plication.descShort: The stomach is folded and stitched — nothing is removed.
plication.meta: Stay [X days] · Back to work [X weeks]

balloon.name: Gastric balloon
balloon.desc: A soft balloon placed by endoscopy for a set period — a first step for patients who need moderate weight loss.
balloon.descShort: Placed by endoscopy for a set period, no surgery.

Procedures.notSure: Not sure which one fits you? That is exactly what the first consultation is for.

Doctor.name: Dr. Mohsen Karam
Doctor.bio: [Draft for Dr. Karam's approval] I graduated in medicine from Alexandria University, completed my Master of Surgery there and became a Fellow of the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland in 1999. For 25 years I practised at Hamad Medical Corporation in Qatar, joining its bariatric and metabolic surgery team in 2013 and working as a consultant from 2018, while teaching residents and fellows and publishing research on sleeve gastrectomy outcomes and safety. At Delta Bariatric Center I bring that experience home to Alexandria, with a team that stays with every patient long after surgery.
Doctor.bioShort: [Draft for approval] Alexandria graduate and FRCSI, with 25 years at Hamad Medical Corporation in Qatar and bariatric surgery since 2013. Now practising in Alexandria with a team that stays with every patient.

Bmi.title: Could weight-loss surgery be right for you?
Bmi.lead: Body Mass Index is one of the first things we look at. Enter your height and weight for a quick indication.

messages.low: Surgery is usually not indicated at this BMI. We are happy to talk through other options with you.
messages.mid: You may qualify for the gastric balloon or, with related health conditions, for surgery.
messages.high: You may be a candidate for bariatric surgery. A consultation will confirm the right option.

Bmi.note: An indication only, not a medical diagnosis.

candidate.q: Am I a candidate for bariatric surgery?
candidate.a: Generally, adults with a BMI of 35 or more, or 30 or more with conditions such as type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure or sleep apnea, may qualify. Dr. Karam will confirm after a full assessment.

laparoscopic.a: Yes. Most procedures are performed through small keyhole incisions, which means less pain, smaller scars and a faster recovery.

stay.q: How long will I stay in hospital?
stay.a: Most patients stay one to three nights depending on the procedure. The gastric balloon is placed and you go home the same day.

work.q: How soon can I return to work?
work.a: Many patients return to desk work within two to three weeks. Physically demanding work may need longer.

after.a: You follow a staged diet with our nutrition team and attend regular follow-up visits so we can track your progress.

After graduating from Alexandria University I spent 25 years at Hamad Medical Corporation in Qatar, where I joined the bariatric and metabolic surgery team in 2013 and worked as a consultant from 2018.
